title: Everyday Pay Card Cashback Program Terms, Statement Payment Amount
content:
# Cartwise Shopper Payouts: Everyday Pay Card Cashback Program Terms

## Clause S. The statement payment amount

**S.1 What a statement payment pays.** On an Everyday Pay Card plan of Cartwise Shopper Payouts, a statement payment pays onto the card the cashback earned and not yet paid for every statement month whose payment day has come, and it carries the latest such month.

**S.2 The cashback still to be paid.** The card's cashback still to be paid is the card cashback balance shown on the account. Every cashback earning raises it; every cashback payment booked on the account, bonuses included, lowers it; it is cleared when the card's cashback lapses; and it never falls below zero. Where the balance shown is higher than the cashback earned less every cashback payment booked on the account, the lower of the two figures is the balance. Whatever the cap leaves unpaid stays in that balance and falls due on the next payment day.

**S.3 The waiting month.** A statement month's earned entries are booked on the first day of the following month, and the month's payment day is that month's cashback payment day (the card plan's cashback payment day of the following month). The latest month with earned entries is therefore still waiting while fewer days than one less than the payment day have passed since its entries were booked.

**S.4 The amount.** The statement payment takes the card cashback balance, leaves out the latest month's earned cashback while that month is still waiting (the result, never below zero, is the cashback due), caps what remains at the monthly cashback cap of the card plan, and pays it rounded to the cent.

**S.5 When a payment is owed.** A statement payment is owed only when the cashback due is at least the card plan's minimum cashback payment. A smaller amount stays in the balance and no payment is made.

The monthly cashback cap, the cashback payment day and the minimum cashback payment are figures of each card plan and are read from the plan's cashback schedule.

## S.6 Reading the waiting test

| Days passed since the latest month's earned entries were booked | Compared with one less than the payment day | That month's cashback |
|---|---|---|
| Fewer | below | left out of this payment (still waiting) |
| Equal or more | not below | included in this payment |

With a payment day on the 5th, one less than the payment day is 4: entries booked on the 1st are still waiting on the 2nd, 3rd and 4th (1, 2 and 3 days passed) and are included from the 5th (4 days passed).

## S.7 Worked illustration (hypothetical figures only)

The following inputs are invented for illustration and are not the figures of any plan or shopper: a monthly cashback cap of 30.00, a cashback payment day on the 5th, a minimum cashback payment of 1.00; a balance shown of 52.40, cashback earned in total 180.00 and cashback payments booked in total 130.00; the August month earned 12.60, booked on 1 September.

1. Cashback still to be paid: the lower of 52.40 and 180.00 less 130.00 (50.00) is 50.00.
2. On 3 September, 2 days have passed, fewer than 4, so August is still waiting: the cashback due is 50.00 less 12.60, which is 37.40.
3. 37.40 is at least 1.00, so a payment is owed.
4. Capped at 30.00, the payment is 30.00, carrying July, the latest month whose payment day has come; 7.40 of July's cashback and August's 12.60 stay in the balance.

On 5 September, 4 days have passed, so August is no longer waiting: the cashback due is 50.00, the payment is 30.00 and it carries August. Had the cashback due been 0.80, no payment would be made and the 0.80 would stay in the balance.
